rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and Methods / Results (Figures 1-8): authors report their own laboratory experiments on hydrogen nanobubble water properties, in vitro ROS removal, and Cu toxicity, ROS levels, enzyme activities and gene expression in Tetrahymena thermophila.
rows.notes: The study is a laboratory toxicology/chemistry study of hydrogen nanobubble water scavenging reactive oxygen species and alleviating copper-induced oxidative stress in a single-celled ciliate. It contains no drip irrigation, no aerated drip irrigation, no crop, no yield or crop quality measurement. It provides no evidence on crop production under drip/ADI; at most it is loosely related to the nanobubble component of aerated/nanobubble irrigation water.

rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and Methods / Results (Figures 1-8): own laboratory experiments on hydrogen nanobubble water, ROS removal in vitro, and Cu-stress responses of Tetrahymena thermophila.
rows.notes: No drip or aerated drip irrigation system, no crop, no pests or pesticides are studied. The study shows hydrogen nanobubble water removes H2O2, O2.- and .OH in vitro and reduces Cu toxicity and endogenous ROS in a ciliate; nothing about reducing pesticide applications or nutrient over-consumption under drip irrigation.

notes: Full text appears complete (abstract through references). The study (Environ. Sci. Technol. 2022) is a cell-level laboratory study of hydrogen nanobubble water antioxidant effects, not an irrigation study; it does not match either claim's technology (drip/ADI) or effects (yield, quality, pesticide reduction).
